title: 71 Forage Basics: Educational Impact of Free, Online Extension Education Course in Alabama Cooperative Extension System
content:
Abstract
Forage Basics is a free online educational program offered by the Alabama Cooperative Extension System (ACES) Animal Science and Forage Team since 2021. The course was developed to assist producers in making informed management decisions when addressing issues related to forage production, sustainability, economics, and livestock management on their farms. The course aimed to reach a wider audience of non-traditional and beginning producers by allowing access to research-based information at no cost. Forage Basics consists of 20 modules on the Canvas (Instructure Holdings Inc., Salt Lake City, Utah) educational platform that can be completed at participants’ own pace and covers a range of relevant topics including forage establishment, soil fertility and environmental amendments, grazing management, establishment budgets, the economics of grazing and hay production, and more. Course content was developed by an interdisciplinary team of research and Extension professionals at Auburn University and the ACES network and promotion of the course was conducted through social media resources, Extension and industry email lists, and in-person contacts at several Extension and commodity meetings. Content within each module was delivered using multiple forms of media including images, videos, text, and interactive graphics. Each module included a short, 3-5 question pre- and post-assessment to measure change in knowledge among participants. In its nearly three-and-a-half year lifespan, Forage Basics has been accessed by 663 participants. Of the participants who accessed the course, 64% completed all available modules. A significant increase in score between the pre and post assessments was observed in 11 out of 20 modules. These preliminary results suggest that Forage Basics had a positive impact on participants’ knowledge level of the course content. Further demographic and background data of participants is needed to inform areas of improvement for the course and methods to fill existing gaps in knowledge among the target population.
